summary.goal: Protect the back, strive upstairs. Six weeks: W5 peaks with squat 365x3 plus two 275x3 backoffs and sumo held at 295; W6 deloads into Korea travel. Loaded hinges stay cut.
changes: GRADED CLEARANCE (2026-08-28): W4 used 275 after the initial 25% instruction. ATHLETE DECISION (2026-09-05): keep the deliberate W5 365 squat peak; W6 is the travel deload. This is a specific exception to the back-check progression gate, not new clinical clearance.
Squat: W1-W3 225x5; W4 275x5; W5 365x3 @7 cap plus 275x3 x2 @6; W6 225x5 x3 @6; W6 runs two days only — D1 squat/bench/pull-up, D2 sumo/dip.
Sumo: W1-W3 225x3; W4 prescribed 275x3; W5 held at 295x3 x3 @6; W6 225x3 x3 @6 on D2 (Tue).
CUT for the window: Paused RDL (loaded hinge) and Paused Low-bar Squat (2nd weekly axial session). Neither is worth its risk right now.
Weighted Back Extension moved D4 -> D2 and held at BODYWEIGHT through W2 — the injections go into these exact muscles. Skip it if the sites are sore.
Bench, pull-up and dip UNCHANGED — full strive plan. No shoulder injection was given (2026-08-07), so masked-pain-load-cap does not bind them.
Comp bench W4 stays a range with 'work up to @8' (255-270x2) — the fix for B4's @6 peak.
Deliberate exception to primary-backoff-volume: squat/sumo volume is cut below the logged norm. A medical restriction outranks a volume rule.
accessory_changes: COVERAGE AUDIT (2026-08-07, rule muscle-coverage-audit): checked all four days against every major group. Found three real holes — lateral delts (nothing trained them), biceps (Concentration Curl had been cut, leaving zero direct work), and core (D2 only). All three now closed.

CALVES IN (2026-08-07, athlete's call) — Seated Calf Raise on D4, SWAPPED for Incline DB Press rather than added, so D4 stays at 21 sets (it was already the longest day). Seated, not standing: zero spinal load. Bonus — it removes a fourth pressing exposure from a shoulder with bursitis and two partial-thickness tears. Log median 175 over 4 sessions. Every major muscle group is now covered.

CORE ON EVERY DAY, four DIFFERENT patterns so they aren't redundant: Side Plank (D1, anti-lateral-flexion) / Pallof Press (D2, anti-rotation) / Dead Bug (D3, anti-extension) / Bird Dog (D4, spine-neutral endurance). All anti-movement work — NO loaded lumbar flexion (cable crunch, sit-ups) and NO hanging leg raise while the back is under treatment (hip-flexor dominant; the psoas attaches onto L1-L5).

D1 SLIMMED to 3 accessories: Skullcrusher CUT (triceps were over-served by pushdown + dip + three bench variants) and Hip Thrust MOVED to D3. D1 was leg- and tricep-heavy; it now runs Leg Press, Tricep Pushdown, Side Plank.
D3 FILLED OUT 3 -> 5 accessories (it was the thinnest day): gains Hip Thrust + Dead Bug.

NEW: Lateral Raise (D2) — the one shoulder head nothing else trains. Log median 40 over 68 sessions, but prescribed at 30-35 DELIBERATELY BELOW it: the MRI shows subacromial bursitis and 60-120 degrees of abduction is exactly this movement's arc. STOP AT SHOULDER HEIGHT, light, high-rep.
BACK IN: Concentration Curl (D4) — cutting it left the biceps with no direct work at all. Log median 38 over 93 sessions. On D4 because nothing follows Friday.

D1 vs D2 balance: 3 accessories vs 5, but ~18 vs ~19 total working sets — D1 carries TWO primary lifts (9 primary sets) to D2's one (4). Balanced by volume, not by count. D1 also structurally can't hold back/biceps work: Mon->Tue is back-to-back into pull-up day.
Hip Thrust on D3 is glute work the day before sumo — acceptable ONLY because sumo is 225 @6 technique work. If Friday's pull feels heavy or the next-day back check is off, it moves to D2.
CALVES remain the one uncovered group — deliberate, not an oversight: zero logged history, no Big-5 carryover, and a medical window is the wrong time to add an unfamiliar movement.

NEW (2026-08-07): Leg Press (D1, replaces Leg Extension — HARD ROM RULE, stop before the pelvis tucks), Hip Thrust (D3), Bulgarian Split Squat (D4, 50 logged sessions). Non-axial leg work replacing the stimulus the axial cap removed.

OUT: Iso-Lateral Row (D1->D2 interference) · Hip Adduction (flat at 115, D3->D4 interference) · Meadows Row (lumbar load on deadlift day) · BW AMRAP (three blocks, never produced a usable number) · Leg Extension (replaced by Leg Press) · Hanging Leg Raise (replaced by the core cluster) · Skullcrusher (triceps redundancy).
MOVED: Face Pull D4 -> D3 (shoulder-health cluster on dip day). Weighted Back Extension D4 -> D2, bodyweight through W2 — the trigger-point injections went into these exact muscles.
RE-ANCHORED from the log (sheet-load-sync): Reverse Pec Deck 45->100, DB Shoulder Press 50->70, Concentration Curl 25->40, Incline DB Press 50->65.

exercises.notes: LIGHT — 4-week back-protection window (doctor, 2026-08-07). 225 FLAT, no weekly ramp: you asked for a higher floor, so you get a higher floor and a LOWER ceiling (was 185->245). ~48% of your 465. 4 sets, not more reps — extra work comes from sets done FRESH, never from fatigued reps. This is POSITION WORK. Do NOT add weight.
exercises.hold_reason: Doctor ordered 4 weeks off heavy lifting (2026-08-07). Light position work only until ~2026-09-04.

exercises.name: Comp Bench
exercises.notes: Top @7. PRIORITY LIFT — strive. ≤3/10 shoulder pain, always. MRI (2026-08-07) confirms low-grade partial tears, no full-thickness, no fatty atrophy — the strive is supported.

exercises.name: Comp Bench
exercises.notes: Backoff — 4 sets @6.

exercises.name: Leg Press (Machine)
exercises.notes: NEW — replaces Leg Extension. Quad/glute volume with no bar on your back. HARD ROM RULE: stop the sled well before your hips lift off the pad — at depth the pelvis tucks under load, and loaded lumbar flexion is exactly the L3-4 mechanism. Run at 315-365, well under your 495 log median: 'moderate if tolerated' is a number here, not a feel, because the injections mask the feel.
exercises.hold_reason: Deliberately prescribed under the log (315-365 vs a 585 log anchor) for the medical window: the ROM rule is what protects the L3-4 protrusion, and the anesthetic masks the feel. Do not let the log rebase this.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown
exercises.notes: Lockout for bench. Log anchor 53 lb.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: CORE (D1) — anti-lateral-flexion. Every day carries one core movement, each a DIFFERENT pattern. Isometric HOLD, 30-40 SECONDS PER SIDE (logged as duration, not reps). Spine neutral, zero spinal compression. Do it in your rest periods between bench sets.

exercises.name: Weighted Pull-up
exercises.notes: Top @7. @8 is still a HARD STOP — it's what fixed this lift.

exercises.name: Weighted Pull-up
exercises.notes: Backoff — 3 sets @6.

exercises.name: Weighted Back Extension
exercises.notes: Erector capacity, NO spinal compression. BODYWEIGHT ONLY through W2 — the trigger-point injections went into these exact muscles, so loading them fresh is not smart. SKIP ENTIRELY if the injection sites are sore. Moved D4 -> D2 (replaces Paused RDL).
exercises.hold_reason: Bodyweight through W2 — trigger-point injections went into these exact muscles (2026-08-07). Do not let the log rebase this.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.notes: Hamstrings / posterior chain with ZERO spinal loading — this is what replaces Paused RDL for the window, and why a DB RDL was declined: you already hinge on D4 (light sumo), and a second loaded hinge is the thing we removed. Log median 115.

exercises.name: DB Shoulder Press
exercises.notes: @7 CAP — shoulder. Overhead is the most bursitis-provocative pattern you own (MRI: mild subacromial-subdeltoid bursitis). Stop on any PAINFUL ARC — pain through the middle range that eases overhead. Two sessions running with that = tell coach, swap to neutral-grip/landmine. Re-anchored 50 → 70.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise (Dumbbell)
exercises.notes: Lateral delts — the one shoulder head nothing else in this block trains (presses hit front, face pull + pec deck hit rear). Log median 40 lb over 68 sessions, but prescribed at 30-35 DELIBERATELY: the MRI shows subacromial bursitis, and 60-120° of abduction is the impingement arc this movement lives in. STOP AT SHOULDER HEIGHT, no higher, light and high-rep. Any painful arc — stop the set and tell me.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.notes: CORE (D2) — anti-rotation. Replaces Hanging Leg Raise, which is hip-flexor dominant; the psoas attaches straight onto L1-L5, so it pulls on the exact segments under treatment. Log median 20 lb. Per side, slow, brace and resist the rotation.

exercises.name: Weighted Dip
exercises.notes: @7. Strive this block. DEPTH IS THE PRIMARY VARIABLE — stop above the pinch point (MRI: subacromial bursitis + AC degeneration compress at the bottom). Full depth buys nothing.

exercises.name: CGB
exercises.notes: NEW on D3 (your ask) — third bench exposure of the week, run as SUPPORT not a strive lift. Close grip on purpose: less shoulder abduction than a comp grip, so less subacromial provocation, and it trains the lockout — the part of your bench that actually fails. Fixed load, @7 cap, elbows tucked. Log median 205; this is deliberately under it. STOP if shoulder pain >3/10.
exercises.hold_reason: Third weekly pressing exposure on a shoulder with two partial-thickness tears + bursitis, on the same day as the dip and the day before Spoto. Deliberately below the 205 lb log median — the sync must not chase it up.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust (Smith Machine)
exercises.notes: RE-ANCHORED 2026-08-11 — the 'empty bar, 0 logged sessions' premise was a name-mapping miss. You have SIX barbell sessions (median 225, max 275x12) and a Smith session at 225x8 (2026-05-26). Running it on the SMITH this block, your call. 205 to re-enter the pattern after ~2.5 months off it. Ribs down, chin tucked, finish with the GLUTES — never hyperextend the low back at lockout. A numb back will not warn you, which is the one reason this is still the cautious end of your history.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.notes: Lat width for the pull-up.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.notes: RE-ANCHORED 45 → 100 (log median 100). You skipped this 4/4 in B4 — it was prescribed at less than half your working load. Posterior-cuff/scap support for the torn anterior tendons; keep it.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.notes: Shoulder health — LOAD-BEARING, not filler. Posterior cuff is intact while supraspinatus/subscapularis are torn, so this shares load off them. High rep, never heavy. Do not cut when short on time.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.notes: CORE (D3) — anti-extension. Teaches the brace that keeps the lumbar spine neutral under load, which is the whole game right now. Bodyweight, per side, slow — lower back stays flat on the floor. If it arches off the floor, shorten the range.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
exercises.notes: LIGHT technique pull — 225 FLAT, 3 sets of 3, no ramp. Triples stay triples: the lever is LOAD and SETS, never reps (rule sumo-back-cap).
